newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shares seen edging up in subdued activity.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares seen edging up in subdued activity.

text.p: Indian shares are likely to drift into positive territory in the week ahead on some increased institutional buying, but brokers and analysts say a sharp movement in prices is unlikely.
"Pivotal stocks look better on renewed buying by local institutional investors," said dealer Mehul Patel at Mukesh Babu Financial Services.
The Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) top 30-share index rose 72.36 points, or 2.36 percent, to 3,139.02 in the week to Friday after falling 184 points in the past two weeks.
Analysts said the market was largely trader-driven, with a lack of market-moving news holding prices in a narrow band.
"The technical position of the market (in the week ahead) is 'up to sideways'. We expect the market to be in the range of 3,275-3,100 points," Nucleus Securities said in a report.
Himanshu Kaji, chief executive at broking firm Mangaldas L Kaji, said he expected the market to make some gains, but foresaw no fireworks.
"I see the Sensex moving in a 50-100 point trading range," he said.
Asked for his assessment of the week ahead, Ramdeo Agarwal, research head at brokers Motilal Oswal said: "I am slightly bullish ... we could see an upward trend on a strong technical position."
Last week, market activity at the BSE focused on shares of tobacco giant ITC which climbed about seven percent to close at 271.75 on the back of hectic short-covering by speculators.
Traders said the sharp backwardation charges attracted by ITC at the close of BSE's weekly account would ensure the trader-driven buying would continue in the week ahead.
Backwardation is a charge on short-sellers to carry forward transactions from one settlement to another.
"This indicates that there are heavy oversold positions in the market ... players will have to rush to cover positions," said Agarwal.

Indian authorities are investigating ITC's role in a $100 million foreign exchange scandal. The Enforcement Directorate, India's corporate watchdog, has arrested several senior ITC officials, as well as two former chairmen, in investigations into alleged violations of foreign exchange rules.

On Friday, an ITC spokeswoman said the firm had suspended its panel of directors after a board meeting in Calcutta. A statement from ITC said the firm's board would be strengthened over the next few weeks by the induction of three independent non-executive directors.
The week ahead sees top firms including Hindalco, Indian Rayon, Colgate, Grasim, Larsen & Toubro and Tata Chemicals report their first-half results for the year ending September 30.
Analysts say they are not reading much into the results, which are generally expected to show a slowdown.
"The market has largely discounted the results ... it is not really receptive to the announcements," said Agarwal.
